newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Mar 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Mar 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh's parliamentary chief whip Abul Hasnat Abdullah, now visiting the Indian state of Tripura, said repatriation of tribal refugees would begin soon.
Forest and Environment Minister Syeda Sajeda Chowdhury told parliament on Sundat that steps had been taken to check air and sound pollution in four major cities including Dhaka.
Former president Hussain Mohammad Ershad said on Sunday that presidential form of government was more suitable for a country like Bangladesh than parliamentary form.
The next round of peace talks with tribal insurgents begins in Dhaka on March 12.
Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad leaves for Pakistan on Monday on a two-day visit to develop rapport with new government of Pakistan.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has appointed Dr S A Malek, an elderly leader of ruling Awami League, as her political adviser.
An eight-member delegation of the Japanese government arrives in Dhaka on Monday to discuss with the government fresh Japanese development loans.
Bangladesh produces 90,000 bales of cotton against the annual demand of 0.55 million bales, Agriculture MInister Begum Matia Chowdhury told the parliament on Sunday. REUTER
